answer: The protocol issues a lightweight lantern challenge: each agent must submit a short computational sketch that, when combined with a time‑varying spiral seed, produces a unique hash recorded on‑ledger. Nodes verify that the hash does not match any existing vine of prior submissions, rejecting duplicates or near‑duplicates instantly. An attacker must generate a fresh, statistically independent output for every new seed, costing linear CPU cycles and storage per identity.
